summary.headline: Hexagon Nutrition Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 43.2% YoY to INR104.3 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.3% from 13.8%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 43.2% YoY to INR104.3 crore, with volume growth of roughly 25-40% across premix and branded segments. EBITDA rose 17.3% to INR11.8 crore, but margin compressed about 250 bps to 11.3% on higher raw material costs (West Asia crisis) and elevated selling, distribution and freight spend. PAT grew 25.1% to INR8.1 crore. Management guided FY27 growth of 20-25%, flagged a INR100 crore order book for Q2-Q3, and said MRP increases of 10-15% on some branded products will help margins from Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Contracted by more than 3 percentage points YoY
financial_highlights.change: Attributed to raw material cost rise

segments.name: Premix (micronutrient)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 62% of Q1 revenue; grew about 55% YoY per CFO. Over 50% of plant capacity utilisation is attributed to premix, and the INR100 crore order book is about 70-75% premix and ESG combined.

segments.name: Branded (clinical/wellness, B2C)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 28% of revenue; grew about 22% YoY (CFO) or about 28% (Dr. Nikhil). Branded share rose from 18% to 20%, 25% and about 30% over recent years. Target of 35% of revenue in the next couple of years; B2C revenue has crossed INR100 crore per an analyst question.

segments.name: Therapeutic nutrition / ESG (RUTF, RUSF, MNP)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 10% of revenue; grew about 42% YoY. Tender-based, so order flows vary quarter to quarter. ESG pipeline cited at INR75-100 crore for the remaining year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at about 20-25%, same trajectory as last year; management called this the conservative side.
Q2 supported by an order book of about INR100 crore, to be executed in Q2 and partly in Q3.
Seasonality: Q1 and Q2 build momentum, with the main growth in Q3 and Q4 per management.
MRP increases of 10-15% on some branded products will affect margins from Q2; gross margin expected to ease over the next two quarters.
Field force investment (over 50% increase YoY) expected to show productivity in roughly two to three quarters, with operating leverage by end of Q3.
Nashik premix facility redevelopment capex of INR25-30 crore over one to one-and-a-half years; about 70% to be funded by long-term bank borrowing.
capex_capacity: Blended capacity utilisation about 47% (rising from around 30% previously stated); management cautioned segment rates vary, with some lines at 35-40% and others around 65%.
Nashik about 55-60% utilised, Tuticorin about 35-40%, Chennai about 25-30%; Uzbekistan has limited order book for Q2-Q3 and is not material yet.
Nashik premix facility being demolished and rebuilt; capex INR25-30 crore over the next 1-1.5 years.
Management says manufacturing capacity suffices for the next two to three years of growth.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of roughly 25-40% YoY in Q1 across premix and branded; management said price hikes were not the main driver.
Raw material cost pressure: about 25-30% of raw materials are imported; whey protein costs rose sharply, while some vitamins were stable.
Freight costs rose due to the West Asia situation; West Asia is under 20% of exports.
Export concentration: top 3-5 countries make up about 25-40% of exports; growth in Central Asia and Africa, with Europe and North America targeted.
Branded MRP raised 10-15% on some products to pass on raw material costs.
Inventory build partly strategic due to rising product prices and ESG/premix order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a slowdown expected given 43% Q1 growth versus 20-25% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nikhil said Q2 is supported by a INR100 crore order book, with no sign of slowdown; Q1 and Q2 build momentum and Q3-Q4 carry the main growth. CFO called 20-25% the conservative side.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin contract, and will it normalise from Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed a more than 3 percentage point gross margin contraction to West Asia-driven raw material cost increases in premix and branded. Management is passing costs to customers via MRP increases and hopes margins normalise from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly freight costs from the geopolitical situation, plus field force and marketing investment; over 50% more field force versus last year, treated as an investment that will pay off in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and its timing?
qa_highlights.answer: INR100 crore order book, to execute in Q2 and partly Q3; about 70-75% premix and ESG, rest branded.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and what is the bottleneck?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended utilisation about 47% (40-47% range cited); premix in 25 kg bags versus branded sachets and tins take different times, so segment-level rates vary widely.

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest constraints to growth over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Nikhil said manufacturing capacity and working capital are not constraints; distribution expansion into Tier 2-3 cities is the focus, with operating leverage expected in a couple of quarters.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression (11.3% vs 13.8%) persists if raw material and freight costs stay high or MRP hikes lag.
Inventory days rose to about 142 from about 130+; strategic stocking may tie up working capital.
Tender-based ESG orders create quarter-to-quarter volatility.
Field force and distribution costs ahead of productivity; leverage expected only by end of Q3.
Branded share target of 35% of revenue in a couple of years; growth needs to keep pace with 20-25% guidance.
West Asia geopolitical risk on freight, raw material costs and exports.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and order book, but defensive on margin compression, attributing it to temporary raw material and freight costs and promising recovery from Q2 with hedges such as "hopefully". Answers on capacity utilisation were detailed but caveated, and the call had some audio disruptions.
